AGENTS.md.excerpt:
Use `npm run typecheck` for type checking. Before you finish a change, run `npm test`, then the `verify` skill on the agent × sandbox combination it touches.

`tsc` is TypeScript 7 (the `@typescript/native` alias of `typescript@7`). The `typescript` package name is an alias of `@typescript/typescript6`, because TypeScript 7 has no JS API and tsup's declaration build still `require`s one. Don't import `typescript` in our own code, and drop the alias once tsup no longer needs it.

Releasing: before merging the changesets **Version Packages** PR, run `npm run test:local` (real Docker and Podman; CI never runs it). See [docs/agents/releasing.md](./docs/agents/releasing.md).

Check [./GLOSSARY.md](./GLOSSARY.md) for terminology questions.

For user-facing changes, add a changeset to `.changeset`. Check all changesets there first to see if there are duplicates. We use `@changesets/cli`, but you can create/edit the file manually. Make all bugfixes `patch`, all new features or breaking changes `minor` (since we're pre-1.0). Use `package.json#name` for the name.

When changing public-facing behavior, check the user docs in `docs/guide/` to see if they need updating.

## User docs

The user docs are the markdown pages in `docs/guide/`. [aihero.dev/sandcastle](https://www.aihero.dev/sandcastle) renders them as a docs site, and `README.md` links to them.

- One page per major term in `GLOSSARY.md`, at `docs/guide/<slug>.md`, with its related terms folded in. The file name is the page's URL: `docs/guide/prompts.md` is `aihero.dev/sandcastle/prompts`. The first line is the page's `# Title`, and its sections are `##` and below.
- A term page opens with a short runnable example, then the details, then a `## Related terms` list of links. It does not repeat definitions: those live on one page.
- `docs/guide/glossary.md` (last in the `Reference` group) defines each user-facing term for readers, one `## Term` entry each, in alphabetical order. It is hand-written, not copied: `GLOSSARY.md` stays the agents' source, and each entry's name must be a term `GLOSSARY.md` defines. When a term is added, renamed or changes meaning in `GLOSSARY.md`, update its entry.
- On every other guide page, the first mention of each glossary term links to its entry (`[worktrees](./glossary.md#worktree)`). A mention is the entry's name, whole word, case-insensitive, plural allowed (`-s`, `-es`, `-y` to `-ies`), outside code, headings and other links; a hyphen joins words, so `no-sandbox` is not a mention of `sandbox`, and a longer term wins, so `agent provider` is not a mention of `agent`. If a word is a mention by these rules but means something else (an interactive "prompt"), reword it.
- Explain each term once in the guide, at its home: its first mention on the earliest page in `toc.json` order that mentions it. Weave one or two plain sentences into the prose there (keep the link); every other page only links it. Each glossary entry ends `First explained in [<Page title>](./<page>.md).`
- Never reference ADRs from the user docs (`docs/guide/`, `README.md`): no `docs/adr/` links, no "ADR 0018". Keep any reasoning a reader needs in plain words.
- The `toc.json` groups follow `GLOSSARY.md`'s groups. The start page (`getting-started`) and the `Reference` group (`run`, every `RunOptions` option and result field, `cli`, and `glossary`) are not term pages. Each option is explained on its term page, and listed once in the reference.
- `docs/guide/toc.json` orders and groups the pages for the sidebar. `start` is the page a new reader opens first. `groups` lists every other page as `{ "title": "...", "pages": ["slug", ...] }`, in sidebar order.
- To add a page, write `docs/guide/<slug>.md`, add its slug to a group in `toc.json`, and link it from the Documentation list in `README.md`. Renaming or removing a page touches the same three places.
- Link between pages with relative paths (`./prompts.md#built-in-prompt-arguments`), and to other repo files relative to the page (`../../src/sandboxes/docker.ts`).
- `tests/docs-guide.test.ts` fails when the three drift apart: a page missing from `toc.json` or `README.md`, a listed page with no file, a page without its `# Title`, a glossary entry whose name `GLOSSARY.md` does not define, a `glossary.md#…` link anywhere in `docs/` or the README to an entry that does not exist, a first mention of a glossary term that is not linked, a glossary entry whose `First explained in` line does not name its home, an ADR reference in the user docs, or a relative link to a file or a guide heading that does not exist.

README.md.excerpt: ## What is Sandcastle? A TypeScript library for orchestrating AI coding agents in isolated sandboxes: 1. You invoke agents with a single `sandcastle.run()`. 2. Sandcastle handles sandboxing the agent with a configurable branch strategy. 3. The commits made on the branches get merged back. Sandcastle is provider-agnostic. It ships with native sandboxes that use your OS's own process sandbox (Bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2, Seatbelt on macOS), image-based providers for Docker and Podman, and cloud providers for Daytona, E2B, Fly.io Sprites, Modal and Vercel, and you can create your own. Great for parallelizing multiple AFK agents, creating review pipelines, or even just orchestrating your own agents. ## Documentation The docs live in [`docs/guide`](./docs/guide), one page per major term, with every term defined in the [Glossary](./docs/guide/glossary.md), and are published at [aihero.dev/sandcastle](https://www.aihero.dev/sandcastle). - [Getting started](./docs/guide/getting-started.md): prerequisites and a quick start - Core: [Core concepts](./docs/guide/core-concepts.md) - Sandboxes: [Sandbox providers](./docs/guide/sandbox-providers.md) - Branching: [Branch strategies](./docs/guide/branch-strategies.md) - Agents: [Agent providers](./docs/guide/agent-providers.md), [Agent sessions](./docs/guide/agent-sessions.md) - Execution: [Iterations](./docs/guide/iterations.md), [Structured output](./docs/guide/structured-output.md) - Prompts: [Prompts](./docs/guide/prompts.md) - Hooks: [Hooks](./docs/guide/hooks.md) - Init: [Init](./docs/guide/init.md) - Display: [Run logs](./docs/guide/run-logs.md) - Reference: [`run()` and `createSandbox()`](./docs/guide/run.md), [CLI commands](./docs/guide/cli.md), [Glossary](./docs/guide/glossary.md) ## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # Bundle with tsup npm test # Run tests with vitest npm run typecheck # Type-check ``` ## License MIT

agent-implement-pr.yml.excerpt:
name: Agent Implement PR

on:
  # pull_request, not pull_request_target: on a fork PR this gets no secrets
  # and a read-only token, so checking out and running the PR's code is safe.
  # Same-repo PRs (the ones the agent opens) keep secrets as before.
  # pull_request does not fire on PRs with merge conflicts (GitHub can't build
  # the merge ref) — resolving those is agent-update-branch's job.
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]

jobs:
  implement-pr:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'agent:implement'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: agent-mutate-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write

    env:
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
      BRANCH_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

    steps:
      - name: Refuse closed PR
        if: github.event.pull_request.state != 'open'
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:implement" || true
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body "Refused to run: PR #${PR_NUMBER} is not open."

      - name: Transition labels
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:implement" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:blocked" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label "agent:in-progress"

      - name: Checkout PR branch
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Prepare branch
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main:main || git fetch origin main
          git checkout "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || git checkout -B "$BRANCH"
          git config user.name "sandcastle-agent[bot]"
          git config user.email "sandcastle-agent[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Setup Node.js
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        run: npm run build

      - name: Install Claude Code
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Run implement-PR agent
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement-pr/implement-pr.ts

      - name: Push branch
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && success()
        run: |
          if [ "$(cat "${RUNNER_TEMP}/has_commits.txt")" != "true" ]; then
            echo "No commits to push."
            exit 0
          fi
          set +e
          git push --force-with-lease="refs/heads/$BRANCH:$BRANCH_HEAD_SHA" origin "$BRANCH" 2> push_err.txt
          status=$?
          set -e
          if [ $status -ne 0 ]; then
            if grep -qiE "non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first|stale info" push_err.txt; then
              echo "Branch advanced during implement-PR run." > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/failure_reason.txt"
              cat push_err.txt
              exit 1
            fi
            cat push_err.txt
            exit $status
          fi

      - name: Post thread replies
        if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && success()
        env:
          REPLIES: ${{ runner.temp }}/implement_thread_replies.json
        run: |
          count=$(jq 'length' "$REPLIES")
          if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
            exit 0
          fi

name: Agent Review

on:
  # pull_request, not pull_request_target: on a fork PR this gets no secrets
  # and a read-only token, so checking out and running the PR's code is safe.
  # Same-repo PRs (the ones the agent opens) keep secrets as before.
  # pull_request does not fire on PRs with merge conflicts (GitHub can't build
  # the merge ref) — resolving those is agent-update-branch's job.
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]

jobs:
  review:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'agent:review'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: agent-mutate-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write

    env:
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
      BRANCH_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

    steps:
      - name: Transition labels
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:review" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:blocked" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label "agent:in-progress"

      - name: Checkout PR branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Prepare branch
        run: |
          git fetch origin main:main || git fetch origin main
          git checkout "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || git checkout -B "$BRANCH"
          git config user.name "sandcastle-agent[bot]"
          git config user.email "sandcastle-agent[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Run review agent
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/review/review.ts

      - name: Push branch
        if: success()
        run: |
          set +e
          git push --force-with-lease="refs/heads/$BRANCH:$BRANCH_HEAD_SHA" origin "$BRANCH" 2> push_err.txt
          status=$?
          set -e
          if [ $status -ne 0 ]; then
            if grep -qiE "non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first|stale info" push_err.txt; then
              echo "Branch advanced during review run." > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/failure_reason.txt"
              cat push_err.txt
              exit 1
            fi
            cat push_err.txt
            exit $status
          fi

      - name: Post PR review
        if: success()
        env:
          PAYLOAD: ${{ runner.temp }}/review_payload.json
        run: gh api --method POST "repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}/reviews" --input "$PAYLOAD"

      - name: Mark PR ready
        if: success()
        run: gh pr ready "$PR_NUMBER" || true

      - name: Post thread replies
        if: success()
        env:
          REPLIES: ${{ runner.temp }}/replies.json
        run: |
          count=$(jq 'length' "$REPLIES")
          if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
            exit 0
          fi
          for i in $(seq 0 $((count - 1))); do
            commentId=$(jq -r ".[$i].commentId" "$REPLIES")
            body=$(jq -r ".[$i].body" "$REPLIES")
            rest_id=$(gh api graphql -f query="query(\$id:ID!){ node(id:\$id){ ... on PullRequestReviewComment { databaseId } } }" -F id="$commentId" --jq '.data.node.databaseId')
            if [ -z "$rest_id" ] || [ "$rest_id" = "null" ]; then
              echo "Could not resolve REST id for $commentId; skipping" >&2
              continue
            fi
            gh api --method POST "repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}/comments/${rest_id}/replies" -f body="$body"
          done

      - name: Mark blocked on failure
        if: failure()

          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}

ci.yml.excerpt:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  # pull_request, not pull_request_target: a fork PR's code runs here with no
  # secrets and a read-only token (see the agent workflows, moved off
  # pull_request_target in 8976368).
  pull_request:
  # The merge queue on main: each queued PR is checked against the PRs ahead
  # of it before it lands.
  merge_group:

permissions:
  contents: read

# A new push to a PR cancels that PR's in-flight run. Runs on main are never
# cancelled: each push to main gets its own group.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Full history: `npm run lint` checks that no baseline grew against
      # origin/main and finds the files a branch changed from its merge-base
      # with origin/main. A default (depth 1) checkout of the PR's merge
      # commit has no origin/main at all; fetch-depth: 0 fetches every branch,
      # so origin/main and a real merge-base are there. With CI set, a missing
      # origin/main fails the lint rather than skipping it.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      # Biome's format check, right after install so unformatted code fails
      # fast, before Bubblewrap, the build or the tests run.
      # Fix locally with `npm run format`.
      - run: npm run format:check
      # bwrap() is proven here under real Bubblewrap (#1272): the containment
      # suite fails, rather than skips, when CI is set and bwrap can't run.
      # Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor blocks the unprivileged user namespaces bwrap
      # needs, so lift that restriction on this throwaway runner.
      - name: Install Bubblewrap
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap
          sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
          bwrap --ro-bind / / true
      - run: npm run typecheck
      # Tests import from dist, so build before test. Lint too: the scripts
      # in .sandcastle/ and .factory/ import @ai-hero/sandcastle, whose types
      # come from dist, so without it type-aware rules see them as any.
      # (Locally, `pretest`/`prelint` build via scripts/ensure-build.ts when
      # dist/ is missing or stale; after this step it is fresh, so they skip.)
      - run: npm run build
      # api-report/ must match the built .d.ts: a public API change shows up
      # in the PR as a report diff, which CODEOWNERS routes to Matt.
      - run: npm run api:report -- --check
      - run: npm run lint
      # `npm test`, split so the e2e tests run once: the floor runs them with
      # coverage, fails on a failing test, and holds their line coverage to
      # scripts/coverage-baseline.json (see scripts/coverage-floor.ts).
      - run: npx vitest run --project tooling --project legacy
      - run: npm run coverage:floor

  # Everything that runs on a real Windows host, in one job: real cmd.exe and
  # Windows argv rules for noSandbox (#940), plus the end-to-end tests
  # (tests/, which include tests/no-sandbox.windows.test.ts). The e2e tests
  # run from src through the vitest alias, so no build is needed — and
  # `npm run build`'s postbuild uses rm/cp, which Windows lacks. Most of the
  # legacy suite assumes a POSIX host (sh, /tmp, POSIX path joins), so only
  # its Windows-relevant file runs here.
  windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      # Coverage for scripts/coverage-gate.ts: code that runs only on win32
      # can count toward deleting a legacy test. The gate merges this artifact
      # with `--coverage-from <dir>` (see the comment at the top of the gate).
      - run: npx vitest run --project e2e --coverage.enabled --coverage.reporter=json --coverage.reportsDirectory=coverage/e2e-windows
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-coverage-windows
          path: coverage/e2e-windows/coverage-final.json
          retention-days: 14
      - run: npx vitest run --project legacy src/sandboxes/no-sandbox.test.ts

lint-shrink.yml.excerpt:
name: Lint shrink baseline

# The lint, test and typecheck ratchets pass when a count falls below their
# baselines (scripts/lint-baseline.json, scripts/test-baseline.json,
# scripts/typecheck-baseline.json), and the e2e coverage floor passes when
# coverage rises above it (scripts/coverage-baseline.json), so fix and
# migration PRs leave them alone. After each push to main this lowers the three
# baselines and raises the floor to what main now has, and opens (or updates)
# one PR with them. It never pushes to main.

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

# A newer push to main supersedes an in-flight run: both would write the same
# branch, and the newer one sees the lower counts.
concurrency:
  group: lint-shrink
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  BRANCH: chore/lint-shrink-baseline
  TITLE: "chore(lint): shrink baseline"

jobs:
  shrink:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # AGENT_PAT, like the agent workflows: a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN
      # does not trigger CI on the PR, so the PR could never go green.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          token: ${{ secrets.AGENT_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      # The type-aware rules need dist (see ci.yml).
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm run lint:shrink
      # Only ever raises the floor. A failing e2e test fails this step but
      # must not hold back the lint baselines.
      - run: npm run coverage:floor -- --raise
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Open or update the shrink PR
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.AGENT_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if git diff --quiet -- scripts/lint-baseline.json scripts/test-baseline.json scripts/typecheck-baseline.json scripts/coverage-baseline.json; then
            echo "Baseline unchanged."
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "sandcastle-agent[bot]"
          git config user.email "sandcastle-agent[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B "$BRANCH"
          git add scripts/lint-baseline.json scripts/test-baseline.json scripts/typecheck-baseline.json scripts/coverage-baseline.json
          git commit -m "$TITLE"
          git push --force origin "$BRANCH"
          body="Lowers \`scripts/lint-baseline.json\`, \`scripts/test-baseline.json\` and \`scripts/typecheck-baseline.json\` to the violations on main at ${GITHUB_SHA}, and raises the e2e coverage floor in \`scripts/coverage-baseline.json\` to its coverage. Generated by \`npm run lint:shrink\` and \`npm run coverage:floor -- --raise\` in the lint-shrink workflow; counts only fall and the floor only rises."
          existing=$(gh pr list --head "$BRANCH" --base main --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number')
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$existing" --body "$body"
          else
            gh pr create --base main --head "$BRANCH" --title "$TITLE" --body "$body"
          fi
